planting.note: Set out rooted semi-hardwood cuttings in spring once frost danger has passed, in a lean, fast-draining spot. Established plants are root-hardy through mild winters in the Gulf South and resprout from the base after a hard freeze knocks back the top growth.

directions: Whitebrush is a wiry, semi-deciduous native shrub of Texas, the Gulf Coast, and northern Mexico in the same genus as lemon verbena, and it shares that cousin's fragrant foliage; the tiny tubular white flowers appear in dense spikes in flushes after rain and are so attractive to bees that ranchers and beekeepers prize the resulting honey. Propagate from semi-hardwood cuttings taken in summer, since seed germination is slow and unreliable, and root them in a well-drained mix before transplanting. Plant in full sun in lean, alkaline, or caliche soils and avoid heavy fertile ground or overwatering, which encourages lank growth and reduces flowering; once established the shrub shrugs off drought and heat with ease. Dry the aromatic leaves for a mild, lemony-anise tisane much as one would with lemon verbena, and prune lightly after bloom flushes to keep the naturally airy, twiggy form tidy.
